# Counts crosswalk — one number, one meaning

**Generated by `scripts/make_counts_crosswalk.py`. Do not hand-edit.**
Canonical freeze: **v1.7.23** (`data/extract_v2/estimates_v1.7.23_frozen.csv`, MD5 `08f050baf45086f45b5b3bec2390a115`).

Five different corpus counts were once simultaneously visible across the manuscript, the PRISMA
diagram, the methods docs and the figures. Each had been correct when written; none was correct
together. This table fixes what each number means so they cannot be conflated again.

| Quantity | Value | Definition |
|---|---:|---|
| Records identified — databases | 30,958 | Scopus + OpenAlex keyword + PubMed + the September behavioural arm, de-duplicated across streams |
| — of which, the three June streams | 25,576 | Scopus + OpenAlex keyword + PubMed, the corpus as it stood before the behavioural arm |
| — of which, the behavioural arm | 5,382 | OpenAlex trace-terms query, run 2026-09-07 |
| Records identified — other methods | 331 | OpenAlex citation snowballing, records advancing to screening |
| Reports sought for retrieval | 1,519 | the reconciliation set; partitioned exactly by terminal states |
| Not retrieved | 145 | documented limitation |
| **Included studies** | **443** | a distinct STUDY contributing >=1 coded estimate |
| **Estimates (all)** | **1,048** | one row per study x country x platform x measure |
| Estimates in the main analysis set | 934 | `value_kind = proportion` and not a demographic subgroup row |
| Studies in the main analysis set | 439 | studies contributing >=1 main-set estimate (some studies hold only subgroup or non-proportion rows) |
| Studies with a risk-of-bias appraisal | 443 | RoB v3, Hoy-adapted; must equal included studies |

## The distinctions that caused the drift

- **Record vs study.** A *record* is one search result. A *study* is one piece of research. The
  reconciliation set (1,519) counts records; the corpus (443) counts
  studies. They can never be compared directly.
- **Study vs estimate.** One study contributes many estimates — a paper reporting four countries
  on two platforms yields eight rows. This is deliberate: within-study variation is the review's
  subject, so "n" is meaningless without saying n of *what*.
- **All estimates vs the main analysis set.** Pooled statistics use only
  `value_kind = proportion` and exclude demographic-subgroup rows, so 934 < 1,048.
  Quality-scale scores, per-capita intensity counts and ranges are stored but never pooled.
- **Superseded counts.** Any figure quoting 408 studies, 695 estimates, 329 studies or 590/680
  estimates predates the current freeze and is wrong for this version. Historical values remain in
  `FROZEN.md` and `research_log.md` on purpose — that is the audit trail, not an inconsistency.

## Drift check
This script also scans current documents for numbers contradicting the table above and fails if it
finds any. Archival files (FROZEN.md, research_log.md, DECISIONS_REGISTER.md, RESUME_HERE.md, counts_crosswalk.md, llm_provenance.md, dataset_provenance.md, v1.2_punchlist.md, v1.2_newrows_worklist.md, blind_reextraction_results.md) are exempt, since they are supposed to record
superseded values.
